events.text: The winter solstice: every family makes dumplings. The saying goes: no dumplings, frozen ears.

effects.log: Your dumplings are shaped like bad decisions. They taste good.
Warm ears all over the lane.

events.text: The longest night of the year. Old people say spirits walk abroad.

choices.text: Keep a lamp burning till dawn

effects.log: Nothing comes. The lamp burns bright.
The darkest night, the stillest mind.

events.text: Families honour their ancestors on the solstice.

effects.log: Incense and quiet words for those before you.
Every master who ever taught you.

events.text: On the longest night, someone knocks at your door. Nobody is there. Then it knocks again.

ok.log: A lost child, too small to reach the knocker properly. You take them home.

fail.log: Only wind, and a very cold hour.

effects.log: The knocking stops at midnight. You never find out.

events.text: An old custom: two masters duel on the solstice to decide who hosts the new year.

effects.log: Two old masters, slow as water, fast as lightning.
An honour, and a nervous hour.

events.text: A soup stall on the corner is giving away mutton soup for the solstice.

effects.log: Hot soup and strangers' laughter.
A thousand bowls. Your arm will never forget.

events.text: Children paint one plum petal a day on a picture of nine nines: eighty-one days until spring.

effects.log: Eighty days to go.

choices.text: Paint one for someone far away

effects.log: You hope they are warm.

events.text: A beggar sits in the snow on the longest night.

effects.log: He sleeps by your fire. He was once a famous sword master.

choices.text: Give him your coat and silver

effects.log: He lives through the night. (−3 taels)

events.text: You are allowed to stay up for the longest night.

effects.log: You make it! Then sleep for a whole day.
You dream of dumplings.

events.text: Standing stones on a hill line up with the solstice sunrise.

effects.log: The light falls exactly between the stones.
The ancients knew more than we think.

events.text: A friend gives you a small gift for the solstice: warm socks, knitted badly.

effects.log: Warm feet, warm heart.
A jar of pickles. They love it.

events.text: After the solstice, the days grow longer. Old masters say this is the moment to start anew.

effects.log: Train every morning. You keep it for almost a month.

choices.text: Write down your regrets and burn them

effects.log: Lighter.
